key_insight: Black participation in landmark hypertrophic cardiomyopathy trials was far below population and site-catchment expectations, with pooled enrollment around one quarter of expected share.
clinical_relevance: Trial underrepresentation can limit how well hypertrophic cardiomyopathy evidence generalizes to Black patients and may help explain persistent outcome disparities.
method: Reviewed 197 registered interventional HCM trials and identified 32 landmark-tier studies.
Extracted race data from 13 trials and pooled Black share among Black and White participants using random-effects meta-analysis.
Compared observed enrollment with US population, site-county catchment, and disease-referenced echocardiographic expectations.
evidence_signal: Across 13 trials, 70 of 1,780 Black or White participants were Black, with a pooled Black share of 3.98% versus a 16.3% population expectation (PPR 0.24).
watch_item: Not all trials reported race, and catchment-based estimates may not capture all real-world referral patterns or other unmeasured barriers to participation.
paper_title: Race and ethnicity in the landmark hypertrophic cardiomyopathy trials: representation against population, site-catchment, and disease-referenced expectations
